preamble: The voiceless alveolar stop [t] becomes the alveolar fricative [s] before a high front vowel (assibilation): the stop gains friction and loses its closure. Finnish changed *t to s before i (*vete > vesi 'water'), and Bantu spirantization turned Proto-Bantu *t into s before the first-degree high vowel *i in Swahili and many other languages.

examples.note: Historical assibilation of t before i.
Bantu spirantization: *t > s before the first-degree high vowel *i
Both stops spirantize; cf. Zulu impisi

sources: Lass, R. (1997). Historical Linguistics and Language Change. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511620928
